Can I get a pin?
Houfeng Didong Yi is the name of the device, invented by Zhang Heng in 132 AD. He was well respected by the court. 
In 138 AD, the device dropped a ball indicating an earthquake west of the capital, Luoyang. Because local residents felt nothing, officials initially doubted it, until a messenger arrived days later confirming an earthquake in that exact direction. 
The device is not a seismograph. It is classified as a seismoscope. This is because it indicated that a quake happened and pointed to its direction, rather than generating a continuous time-record of ground motion.

comments.text:
The narrative of the arrogant emperor laughing, calling it an "expensive toy," and throwing the inventor out of the city is historical fiction for dramatic effect:

Zhang Heng was a prominent, highly respected imperial official and court astronomer, not a mocked outsider living in a hut on a hill. He held prestigious positions in the imperial government.

He explicitly explained how it worked to the court. The device was officially documented in historical texts (like the Book of Later Han). Inside the urn was a pendulum-like inertial mechanism (likely a central column) that would shift when tremors occurred, triggering a lever system to drop a ball.

While historical records do note that people were initially skeptical because no one had ever built an earthquake detector before, that skepticism vanished dramatically. According to historical texts, a ball dropped when no one felt any shaking in the capital, and days later, a messenger arrived reporting a major earthquake hundreds of miles away in that exact direction—proving its accuracy and earning the court's immediate respect.
